claimed_root_cause: CreateJobRequest.input_folder is persisted and later used as a filesystem and R2-namespace selector without the account upload-root chroot that _queued_job_upload_folder already implements, and parse_batch_folder derives tenant from that path rather than from ProcessingJob.account_id.
title: POST /jobs stores an un-chrooted input_folder that process_job rglobs into Gemini and the caller's catalog
description: An authenticated catalogger or owner can POST /jobs with an arbitrary input_folder. Unlike POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files, create_job does not require that path to sit under UPLOAD_ROOT/{account_id}. The row is inserted as queued, so the catalog worker can claim it without a separate unsafe /run trick. process_job then Path.rglob-s image suffixes, may rewrite files in that tree, copies them into catalog/{job.account_id}, and sends them to Gemini. The job row's account_id filter only authorizes who may own the job; it does not isolate the filesystem or R2 batch key. A path equal to the shared upload root or catalog/ subtree therefore selects other tenants' on-disk images. A path shaped as upload_root/{victim_account}/{victim_batch} makes parse_batch_folder restore that tenant's job-batches/ objects using worker R2 credentials.

trace.description: After blocking clients and binding sale_id via _sale_for_user, the handler writes payload.input_folder onto ProcessingJob with status=queued and no UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id relative_to check.
POST /jobs/{id}/run resolves the job by id and account_id, then uses Path(job.input_folder) for R2 staging with no second chroot. create_job already queued the row, so app.worker can also claim it.
account_id and batch_id are taken from the first two path components under upload_root(), not from the job row, then used as the R2 prefix job-batches/{account}/{batch}/.
folder.rglob('*') collects IMAGE_EXTS under the attacker-chosen directory; _add_catalog_photo persists copies under job.account_id and the pipeline sends frames to Gemini.

validation_plan.local: In an isolated dummy two-account fixture with Gemini and R2 mocked, create catalog JPEGs under upload_root/catalog/{B} and a job-batch under upload_root/{B}/{batch}. As catalogger A, insert a ProcessingJob via the create_job request body with input_folder pointing at B's catalog directory and at B's batch directory. Invoke process_job. Confirm A's Photo rows receive B's pixels, B's files may be re-encoded, and restore_job_folder_from_r2 is invoked with job-batches/{B}/{batch}/ rather than A's id. Do not use production data or network.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: inspect one worker replica's backend/data/uploads/catalog layout after mixed-tenant jobs, and confirm application-side R2 list is not additionally scoped by ProcessingJob.account_id. Do not probe a live customer tenant.

Whether a given Railway worker disk currently holds catalog/{other_account} files, and whether R2 list/get on job-batches/* succeeds for a path-derived other account, is a deployment fact outside this source review.

evidence.description: _queued_job_upload_folder is the sibling control: resolve job.input_folder and relative_to(UPLOAD_ROOT/account_id), used only by upload-files, not by create_job.
delete_job only rmtree when the resolved folder is under UPLOAD_ROOT, so destructive cleanup is chrooted while catalog read is not.

claimed_root_cause: Multipart handlers treat UploadFile.read() as the size gate: photos never have a byte budget, and videos check MAX_VIDEO_BYTES only after the full buffer exists. There is no source-visible Starlette/FastAPI max body, per-request file-count cap for batch jobs, or streaming discard.
title: Catalog multipart ingest buffers entire parts in the shared API process with no photo byte cap
description: Restricted clients and staff upload photos through POST /jobs/upload and POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files into save_uploaded_files, which await-reads each UploadFile fully, optionally runs Pillow, writes the bytes, and mirrors to R2. JWT, enforce_client_http, account_id, and assigned-sale checks gate who may call those routes, but they do not bound part size. catalog_limits defines MAX_VIDEO_BYTES and a 40-photo CTBids cap, but no photo-byte ceiling; the 40-file check runs only in single_lot_mode (and only after multipart parse). Lot video upload does have an 80 MiB cap, but only after the entire part is already in memory. FastAPI is constructed with default options (no request-size limit in source; only security-headers, CORS, and optional TrustedHost middleware). Concurrent saves use a semaphore of 12, so several large parts occupy RAM together on the single API process that also serves other tenants' dashboard and pool checkouts.

trace.description: Authenticated client or catalogger posts files: list[UploadFile] with no length or byte Form constraint; CTBIDS_MAX_PHOTOS_PER_LOT applies only when single_lot_mode is true.
body = await uf.read() materializes the entire part. concurrency=12 gather runs many such reads. Pillow compress runs after this allocation; non-image names skip compress and keep raw bytes.
target.write_bytes(body) plus mirror_local_file_to_r2 retain the object on local disk and operator-owned R2. The same process hosts other tenants' HTTP and QueuePool.

validation_plan.local: With Gemini and R2 mocked and strict process memory/time limits, post one oversize JPEG and one oversize non-image part to save_uploaded_files / create_job_from_upload, and one oversize video to upload_lot_videos. Observe that photo parts are fully buffered with no 413, and that video rejection happens only after len(raw) is known. Repeat with a large files list while single_lot_mode is false. Do not stress a shared host beyond the fixture limit.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed: record whether Railway/ingress enforces a request body ceiling in front of the API service, and whether that ceiling applies to multipart parts before uvicorn allocates them. Do not flood the production API.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox is available (empty allowlist env, no-network namespace, read-only target, trusted parent-side no-follow promotion), so peak RSS and disk growth were not measured with a small oversized fixture.
Railway/proxy/client_max_body_size and platform multipart limits are not declared in this repository; an upstream cap would change shared impact and must be owner-observed.
Paid R2 put and Gemini spend from a huge accepted batch were not exercised (mocked-only local check required).

evidence.description: MAX_VIDEO_BYTES is the only ingest byte constant; there is no MAX_PHOTO_BYTES. CTBIDS_MAX_PHOTOS_PER_LOT is a listing count, not a transfer-size cap.
upload_lot_videos does raw = await file.read() then lot_video_size_error(len(raw)), so the advertised 80 MiB bound is after unbounded buffering.
app = FastAPI(title=settings.app_name) installs no max request size, body limit, or upload middleware.
client_http_allowed includes POST /jobs/upload, so the unbounded buffer is reachable by the client role, not only owners.
UPLOAD_FILE_CHUNK = 48 is a browser timeout workaround, not an API cardinality or byte limit; additional chunks append to the same job.

claimed_root_cause: production_must_be_safe is skipped for any non-production ENVIRONMENT, while the in-image default SECRET_KEY and backend/.env.example placeholder remain valid in that mode, and deploy docs start the public API in that mode.
title: Default JWT SECRET_KEY stays accepted whenever ENVIRONMENT is not production
description: The production validator refuses weak SECRET_KEY values, SQLite, and empty CORS_ORIGINS, but only after ENVIRONMENT is production or prod. Settings still default SECRET_KEY to the public placeholder change-me-dev-secret, Dockerfile.api/Procfile do not set SECRET_KEY or ENVIRONMENT, and DEPLOY.md first-time order deploys the API with ENVIRONMENT=development then publishes a domain. If that bootstrap (or a forgotten ENVIRONMENT flip) is live and SECRET_KEY was left unset or set to a documented placeholder, an internet caller can HS256-sign staff JWTs with that key. user_from_access_token still requires a matching active User row (UUID sub plus account_id); the break is issuer impersonation for those existing rows, including re-signing a leaked or expired payload. Live Railway env values were not observed.

trace.description: Documented first deploy sets ENVIRONMENT=development on the API so CORS_ORIGINS is not required; the same order then uses a public API URL and later flips to production.
SECRET_KEY defaults to the well-known placeholder change-me-dev-secret when unset. .env.example is not loaded; the image has no .env.
If environment is not production or prod, the function returns without rejecting weak keys, SQLite, or missing CORS_ORIGINS.
Access tokens are HS256-signed with settings.secret_key and carry sub, account_id, and role with no audience or issuer.
jwt.decode accepts HS256 with settings.secret_key, require_sub, and verify_aud False, then loads User by payload sub plus account_id.

Mint an HS256 token with key change-me-dev-secret for that user's id and account_id (and a second token for a non-existent pair). Confirm user_from_access_token returns the seeded user for the first token and raises 401 for the second. Repeat startup with ENVIRONMENT=production and unset SECRET_KEY and confirm Settings() raises ValueError before the server binds.

claimed_root_cause: Token seal functions catch ImportError and persist unauthenticated XOR under a xor: prefix keyed from SECRET_KEY, and unseal accepts that prefix unconditionally.
title: Facebook and CT Seller sealing fall open to SECRET_KEY XOR when Fernet import fails
description: seal_facebook_secret intends Fernet with a key derived from META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY or SECRET_KEY. If cryptography cannot be imported, it writes xor: plus a repeating XOR of sha256(meta-page:SECRET_KEY), ignoring META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY. unseal_facebook_secret always decrypts xor: blobs with that SECRET_KEY material even when Fernet is available. ctseller.seal_secret has the same ImportError fallback; its XOR key is sha256(SECRET_KEY) without the ctseller: prefix used by Fernet. Dockerfiles install cryptography>=42.0.0, so the branch is a fail-open for a missing or broken import rather than the default image path. API schemas do not return unsealed tokens.

trace.description: Fresh Facebook user and Page tokens are passed to seal_facebook_secret before commit.
Fernet is attempted with sha256(meta-page: dedicated-or-SECRET_KEY).
ImportError stores xor: ciphertext derived only from SECRET_KEY.

validation_plan.local: On an isolated checkout with dummy strings only, monkeypatch cryptography.fernet import to raise ImportError, call seal_facebook_secret and ctseller.seal_secret, assert xor: prefixes, then unseal and compare to the inputs. Set META_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY to a distinct dummy and assert Facebook XOR still follows SECRET_KEY. Restore the import and assert Fernet output has no xor: prefix, then unseal a previously written xor: blob while Fernet imports successfully. Do not call Meta, CT Seller, or a running API.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner-observed only: in the production API and worker images, run a one-shot import cryptography check and SELECT whether any accounts.facebook_user_token_enc, facebook_page_token_enc, ctseller_password_enc, ctseller_access_token_enc, or ctseller_refresh_token_enc values start with xor:. Do not post to Facebook or CT Seller and do not rotate live tokens for this check.

Whether every deployed process (Railway API, worker, and any non-Docker host) can import cryptography is not source-provable.

unseal always handles xor: with SECRET_KEY material.

claimed_root_cause: The callback trusts only decode_oauth_state on a SECRET_KEY HS256 JWT and then complete_oauth writes sealed Facebook tokens without session binding, PKCE, audience, or single-use state.
title: Unauthenticated Facebook OAuth callback writes Page tokens from HS256 state alone
description: GET /integrations/facebook/oauth/callback is unauthenticated. A 15-minute HS256 JWT signed with SECRET_KEY (purpose=meta_oauth, account_id, user_id, exp; no aud, iss, or jti) is enough to exchange a Facebook code and persist user and Page access tokens on the account named in state. There is no PKCE verifier, no one-time state store, and no check that the browser is the owner who called /oauth/start. A signed start URL is therefore a transferable capability: a Facebook admin who completes an attacker-started dialog binds their Page tokens to the attacker tenant, and a stolen owner start URL lets another Facebook user overwrite that tenant's stored Page connection. Staff JWTs are not accepted as state because they lack purpose=meta_oauth. Meta redirect_uri is taken from settings, not Host.

trace.description: Unauthenticated GET receives Facebook code and state and calls complete_oauth.
jwt.decode verifies HS256 and exp with verify_aud False; only purpose, account_id, and user_id are checked.
State account/user are loaded; is_owner is required, but no current Bearer or cookie is required.
Facebook user and Page tokens are sealed onto the state-selected account and committed.

validation_plan.local: With Graph helpers mocked as in test_oauth_callback_stores_encrypted_page_token, GET the callback without Authorization using encode_oauth_state for account A and a dummy code; assert A receives the sealed tokens. Repeat with a staff JWT as state and expect 400. Repeat with account A state while the TestClient is authenticated as a different user and assert tokens still land on A.

blockers: No OS-enforced sandbox and no parent scratch-promotion procedure, so target code was not executed.
Facebook authorization-code single-use, consent-screen behavior, and the deployed Meta Valid OAuth Redirect URIs list are not observable from source.

evidence.description: Callback route declares no Depends(get_current_user).
State claims are purpose, account_id, user_id, iat, exp; no aud, iss, jti, or nonce.
decode options require exp and disable audience verification.
oauth_dialog_url sends code flow without code_challenge.
Staff access tokens use the same SECRET_KEY and also set verify_aud False, but omit purpose.
Unit test completes OAuth and stores a Page token using only code and state.

claimed_root_cause: Engagement ingest accepts unconstrained http(s) item_url/auction_url and later caption builders treat snapshot.item_url as the lot link without a CT Bids host check.
title: Watcher item_url is stored unsanitized and deterministically copied into Gemini Facebook captions
description: A catalogger (Watcher JWT on the same account) can POST /integrations/engagement/snapshots with an arbitrary item_url and auction_url. claimed_root_cause: Lot fields are interpolated as trusted labeled lines into a Google Search tool call with no query/URL allowlist, and hunt JSON URLs are stored after only a javascript:/data: filter.
reason: Cited lines are real at c661a8fd: hunt_lot_audience (backend/app/main.py:5115) calls _require_can_run_audience_hunt; _lot_research_text (backend/app/services/audience_hunt.py:451-479) emits labeled Title/SKU/Description/Specs plus pickup city; audience_research_prompt (511-532) appends that block after instructions; run_audience_research_and_structure (566-575) attaches tools=[GoogleSearch()]; _safe_public_url (205-216) keeps any http(s) string and drops javascript:/data:; recommend_hold at 662-663 can set audience_hold. That is intended same-principal hunt authority plus missing delimiter/host hygiene, not a crossed boundary. The owner is the requester and Gemini billing principal; those lot fields are the designed research subject of Find groups. Cataloggers on the same account already PATCH auction_title, professional_description, specification_lines, sku, and audience_hold (update_lot at backend/app/main.py:4958-5019 blocks only clients). Attacker is a catalogger (or client photos that became listing text) who does not run the hunt. claimed_root_cause: Photo-count enforcement is tied to single_lot_mode plus non-facebook channel, and there is no per-account job-count or Gemini token/$ quota on the shared key.
title: Client and catalogger can stack uncapped batch catalog jobs on the shared operator Gemini key
description: Catalog /jobs/{id}/run is intentionally allowed for catalogger and client on their jobs. The missing bound is cardinality, not the run permission. POST /jobs/upload defaults to single_lot_mode=false, and the 40-photo CT Bids cap is skipped for batch mode and for facebook listing_channel. upload-files repeats that single-lot-only cap. One /run then Flash-triages every file (plus tape-verify and a Pro author pass per tape segment) using the process-wide GOOGLE_API_KEY. Callers can also enqueue an unbounded number of jobs; only catalog_job_max_concurrent (default 1) and gemini_global_concurrency (default 3, shared across tenants) limit in-flight work. Attacker is a client or catalogger. Affected principal is the operator Gemini bill and other tenants waiting on the global Gemini semaphore. Execution identity is the API/worker with the operator key.

Client or catalogger may start their job; no spend quota is checked before queueing Gemini work.
Every uploaded image is sent through triage_ordered_photo_batch (one Flash call per file) before per-segment Pro inventory, billed to the operator key.

Clients cannot appraise; catalog Search is same-principal catalog authority behind an off-by-default flag. title: Master-admin email can be claimed by open registration or team invite
description: All-tenant admin is not a stored role. Any authenticated non-client user whose users.email is in MASTER_ADMIN_EMAILS may list, archive, restore, and delete every Account. Keys are deterministic from account_id plus photo or batch id. R2 CORS AllowedOrigins come from cors_allow_origins (always includes localhost; stars dropped) and are not caller-chosen; CORS does not publish object bytes. Live ACL and public-URL state were not observed and must not be probed.

claimed_root_cause: Maintained Dockerfiles treat mutable tags and unbounded pip specs as the release input, and bake a remotely fetched rembg model into the API image without an integrity pin.
reason: Source confirms the floating tags and unpinned pip path: infra/docker/Dockerfile.api:2 and Dockerfile.worker:4 FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm; Dockerfile.web:2 and :20 FROM node:22-bookworm-slim; requirements.txt uses >= lower bounds (bcrypt alone has <6); Dockerfile.api:10-11 RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt then rembg new_session('u2netp'); worker :12 installs the same file without prefetching the model. That is missing pin/digest hygiene, not a cross-boundary result. There is no lower-trust writer: resolvers use official image names and default PyPI (no extra-index-url, pip.conf, or alternate root), COPY only this repo's requirements.txt, and there is no in-repo CI, cache, or PR job a contributor could poison. The claimed actor is a generic publisher of packages already named in source. The consuming job is the owner's git-push Railway rebuild (DEPLOY.md:11, :194; same-principal). Dockerfile.web:4-5 already lockfiles JS via npm ci. Observing live Railway digests or hashing u2netp would only snapshot current floating resolution; it would not add a distinct writer or an unauthorized path into trusted output.
title: API and worker images consume floating base tags, unpinned PyPI specs, and an unsigned rembg model
description: Each Docker rebuild of Dockerfile.api and Dockerfile.worker runs pip install against requirements.txt lower bounds and pulls python:3.12-slim-bookworm by tag. The API image additionally downloads the rembg u2netp model during build with no checksum. A PyPI or registry publisher who can change a matching version, retag the base image, or replace the rembg model bytes can land code or weights in the next Railway image. Web JS is lockfiled via npm ci; the Node base tag is still floating. Live resolved digests were not observed.

npm ci is the contrasting control: frontend lockfile is copied and used, unlike Python.
Production images are built from repository root using these Dockerfiles, or optionally Procfile/Nixpacks, on each git push.

claimed_root_cause: health() is unauthenticated and serializes upload_root() and _count_catalog_image_files() into HealthResponse, unlike production path redaction used for job input_folder.
reason: Source confirms the unauthenticated serializer: backend/app/main.py:851 health() has no identity Depends; :854-862 returns catalog_upload_root=str(upload_root()), catalog_image_files_on_disk from _count_catalog_image_files() (:836 rglob, cap 200000), catalog_r2_configured, and settings model names. HealthResponse at backend/app/schemas.py:11-19 includes those fields. SecurityHeadersMiddleware, CORS, and optional TrustedHost do not authenticate the route. That is not a meaningful cross-boundary result. upload_root() at backend/app/catalog_storage.py:20-22 is the fixed resolve of backend/data/uploads beside this file. infra/docker/Dockerfile.api:14-16 copies backend under /app and creates backend/data/uploads, so the absolute string is the documented layout. DEPLOY.md:112 already names that cache path; :64 publishes GET /health on the API domain as the liveness probe; :118 documents that the same probe reports catalog_r2_configured. Gemini model defaults are in backend/app/config.py:105-106. The integer file count names no account, file, or tenant object, and the route does not read or serve catalog bytes. public_job_input_folder (backend/app/config.py:247, used only from _job_out at backend/app/main.py:536) redacts per-job input_folder strings for authenticated clients in production; it is not a control on this fixed application directory. Chatty public health JSON is missing probe hygiene, not disclosure of a protected resource. A TestClient GET is not a decisive missing fact: FastAPI serializes the HealthResponse the handler constructs.

catalog_upload_root is the raw absolute path string, not public_job_input_folder.

claimed_root_cause: get_current_user_sse accepts Query access_token as equivalent to Authorization Bearer, and the dashboard EventSource puts that JWT in the URL. Default uvicorn process logging records the request query.
title: Staff JWT placed in EventSource query string; same Query door authenticates catalog uploads
description: A lower-trust observer of API or proxy access logs, or of the HTTP request target, can recover a staff JWT. The dashboard builds EventSource on /jobs/{id}/events?access_token= plus the live token. get_current_user_sse treats Query access_token as equivalent to Authorization Bearer and mints a full User for GET /jobs/{id}/events, POST /jobs/upload, and POST /jobs/{id}/upload-files. First-party upload clients send the JWT in the Authorization header, not the query; the observed client leak is the EventSource URL. Tokens default to 43200 minutes and user_from_access_token does not bind iat to password changes. Procfile and Dockerfile.api start uvicorn without --no-access-log. Whether the running process or Railway edge actually retains the request-target query was not observed.

trace.description: Browser builds /jobs/{id}/events?access_token= plus the staff JWT and opens EventSource on it.
FastAPI Query access_token is documented as the EventSource JWT and is optional beside HTTP Bearer.
Query value is OR'd with Bearer credentials and passed to user_from_access_token, minting a full User principal for SSE and for POST /jobs/upload and /jobs/{id}/upload-files.

validation_plan.local: In the required OS sandbox with dummy tenants, mint a JWT, then start uvicorn (not TestClient) and GET /jobs/{id}/events?access_token=<dummy-jwt> plus POST /jobs/upload?access_token=<dummy-jwt>. Confirm the query door authenticates and that the uvicorn access-log request target contains the access_token query name. Redact token values in any retained log excerpt.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner inspects existing Railway or API access-log settings and any retained /jobs/*/events?access_token= lines; do not replay live tokens or probe production.

blockers: OS-enforced sandbox is unavailable (empty allowlist env, no-network namespace, read-only target, trusted parent-side no-follow promotion); uvicorn access-log request-target capture was not executed.
Live Railway or proxy access-log retention for /jobs/*/events?access_token= is a host-dashboard fact and was not observed; this run must not fetch production.
